results.description: The SCAFFOLD algorithm proceeds over R iterations of the outer loop, with total iterations T = 2Rτ.
results.evidence: In src/reproduction/algorithms.py, run_scaffold() (lines 66-107): with record_every_pair=True (the default experiment mode per configs/fig1_scaffold_delta.json), the outer while loop (line 81) iterates exactly `rounds` (R) times — `completed` is incremented only once per while iteration (line 100). Each iteration performs τ control-variate steps (line 84) and τ corrected local steps (lines 95-97), giving 2τ total per outer iteration and T = 2Rτ overall. The return dict also explicitly records `internal_intervals: rounds * 2` (line 106) when record_every_pair=True, directly encoding the 2R communication intervals consistent with T = 2Rτ.
results.note: When record_every_pair=False, the loop increments `completed` twice per while iteration (lines 87 and 100), so the outer loop runs ~R/2 times — but this mode is not used in the paper's experiments (all SCAFFOLD configs set record_every_pair=true).

results.description: In Algorithm 1 line 3, each worker i computes g̃_{rτ}^i = (1/τ)∑_{j=0}^{τ−1} G_i(x̄_{2rτ}, ξ_{rτ,j}^i).
results.evidence: In src/reproduction/algorithms.py lines 83-84, the run_scaffold function computes per-worker mini-batch gradient estimates: `controls.append(np.mean([_oracle(worker.gradient, x, rng, sigma) for _ in range(tau)], axis=0))`. The `_oracle` call at lines 18-20 returns `worker_gradient(x) + noise`, i.e., a stochastic gradient G_i(x, ξ). The np.mean over `tau` samples gives exactly (1/τ)∑_{j=0}^{τ−1} G_i(x̄_{2rτ}, ξ_{rτ,j}^i), where `x` corresponds to the current global model x̄_{2rτ}.
results.note: The subscript indexing (r, τ) is implicit via Python loop structure rather than explicit variable names, but the mathematical operation is a direct match.

results.description: In Algorithm 1 line 6, each worker i sets ĝ_{rτ}^i = g̃_{rτ}^i.
results.evidence: In `src/reproduction/algorithms.py`, the `run_scaffold` function (lines 82–85) implements Algorithm 1. For each worker i, `controls[i]` is computed on line 84 as `np.mean([_oracle(worker.gradient, x, rng, sigma) for _ in range(tau)], axis=0)`, which is a mini-batch average of stochastic gradient calls. This is the "ĝ_{rτ}^i = g̃_{rτ}^i" assignment: the worker's gradient estimate (control variate) is set directly to the local stochastic gradient, matching Algorithm 1 line 6. The `global_control` on line 85 averages all workers' controls.
results.note: The code uses `controls` as the variable name for ĝ and stochastic gradient calls via `_oracle` as g̃. The tau-sample mini-batch averaging is an equivalent representation of the per-step stochastic gradient if tau=1, or a batched form otherwise. Confidence is medium because the exact paper notation of Algorithm 1 line 6 cannot be directly verified without the paper text, but the SCAFFOLD control variate assignment pattern is clearly present.

results.description: In Algorithm 1 line 10, g̃_{rτ} (without superscript i) is the average of all workers' g̃_{rτ}^i, i.e., g̃_{rτ} = (1/n)∑_{i=1}^n g̃_{rτ}^i.
results.evidence: In src/reproduction/algorithms.py, run_scaffold(): line 84 builds per-worker estimates `controls[i] = np.mean([_oracle(worker.gradient, x, rng, sigma) for _ in range(tau)], axis=0)` (g̃_{rτ}^i), and line 85 computes `global_control = np.mean(controls, axis=0)`, which is the arithmetic mean (1/n)∑_{i=1}^n g̃_{rτ}^i — exactly the global g̃_{rτ} from Algorithm 1 line 10.

results.description: In Algorithm 1 line 10, each worker i updates its local model as x_{2rτ+τ+k}^i = x_{2rτ+τ+k-1}^i − η (G_i(x_{2rτ+τ+k-1}^i, ξ_{2rτ+τ+k-1}^i) − ĝ_{rτ}^i + g̃_{rτ}) for k = 0, …, τ−1.
results.evidence: src/reproduction/algorithms.py lines 93–98 in run_scaffold(): for each worker, local starts at the shared x; then for tau iterations: corrected = _oracle(worker.gradient, local, rng, sigma) - control + global_control; local -= eta * corrected. Here _oracle gives G_i(x,ξ), control is ĝ_{rτ}^i (mini-batch gradient computed in the first interval at lines 83–85), global_control is g̃_{rτ} (mean of controls, line 85), matching exactly x_{...}^i = x_{...}^i - η(G_i - ĝ_{rτ}^i + g̃_{rτ}) for k=0,...,τ-1.

results.description: In Algorithm 1 line 13, the global model is updated by averaging all workers' models: x̄_{2(r+1)τ} = (1/n)∑_{i=1}^n x_{2rτ+2τ}^i.
results.evidence: In src/reproduction/algorithms.py, the `run_scaffold` function (Algorithm 1) at line 99 computes `x = np.mean(local_models, axis=0)`. The list `local_models` is built by appending each worker's final local model after tau corrected local steps (lines 92-98), giving exactly (1/n)∑_{i=1}^n x_i — the global model update described in Algorithm 1 line 13.
results.note: np.mean over axis=0 with n elements computes the arithmetic mean, equivalent to (1/n)∑.

results.description: The simplified SCAFFOLD variant drops partial worker participation, use of the last update for variance reduction, and different local/global stepsizes from the original SCAFFOLD algorithm.
results.evidence: src/reproduction/algorithms.py lines 66-107: The `run_scaffold` function is documented as "Simplified two-round SCAFFOLD used in Algorithm 1 of the paper." (1) All workers participate (`for worker, rng in zip(workers, rngs)`) — no partial participation. (2) Control variates are computed as fresh mini-batch estimates at the current global model `x` (line 84), not using the last local update for variance reduction (SCAFFOLD Option II). (3) Only one stepsize `eta` is used for all local steps (line 97 `local -= eta * corrected`), no separate local/global stepsizes. README.md line 3 and CLAIMS.json line 22 also refer to "the simplified two-round SCAFFOLD variant."
results.note: The rubric describes the simplifications relative to the original SCAFFOLD algorithm from Karimireddy et al. 2020, and all three features (partial participation, last-update variance reduction, different stepsizes) are confirmed absent from the implementation.

results.description: In MbSGD, each worker computes g_t^i = (1/τ)∑_{j=0}^{τ−1} G_i(x_t^i, ξ_{t,j}^i) and updates x_{t+1}^i = x_t^i − η g_t^i.
results.evidence: In src/reproduction/algorithms.py, run_mbsgd (lines 28-43): the batch gradient is computed correctly as np.mean([...tau oracle samples...], axis=0), matching g_t^i = (1/τ)∑G_i. However, the worker update at line 40 is `x - eta * tau * batch`, i.e., x_t^i − η·τ·g_t^i, not x_t^i − η·g_t^i as the rubric requires — there is an extra factor of τ multiplying the learning rate. Additionally, all workers start from the same shared `x` each round (no independent x_t^i per worker), and their outputs are averaged rather than each worker independently updating its own model state.
results.note: The averaging of τ gradients (the g_t^i computation) is correct, but the update step multiplies by tau as well, contradicting the stated formula x_{t+1}^i = x_t^i − η g_t^i.

results.description: In LocalSGD, each worker computes g_t^i = G_i(x_t^i, ξ_t^i) and updates x_{t+1}^i = x_t^i − η g_t^i; if t+1 is a multiple of τ, then x_{t+1}^i = (1/n)∑_{j=1}^n x_{t+1}^j for all i.
results.evidence: src/reproduction/algorithms.py, lines 46-63: `run_localsgd` implements exactly the described algorithm. Lines 56-60: each worker starts from a shared x, takes τ local SGD steps (`local -= eta * _oracle(worker.gradient, local, rng, sigma)`), producing x_{t+1}^i. Line 61: after τ steps, all workers' models are averaged (`x = np.mean(local_models, axis=0)`), matching the "if t+1 is multiple of τ, x_{t+1}^i = (1/n)∑_j x_{t+1}^j" synchronization rule.
results.note: The code uses a rounds-of-τ structure (τ steps, then average, repeat) which is equivalent to the per-step formulation with averaging every τ steps. The gradient oracle (_oracle) injects noise σ consistent with the stochastic gradient G_i(x, ξ) formulation.

results.description: All three algorithms (MbSGD, LocalSGD, SCAFFOLD) assume all workers are initialized with the same point: x_0^1 = … = x_0^n.
results.evidence: In src/reproduction/algorithms.py: run_mbsgd (line 32) sets `x = problem.x0.copy()` and all workers use this shared `x`; run_localsgd (line 50) sets `x = problem.x0.copy()` and each worker starts from `local = x.copy()` (line 57); run_scaffold (line 75) sets `x = problem.x0.copy()` and each worker starts from `local = x.copy()` (line 94). All three algorithms use a single shared initialization point x0 for every worker, satisfying x_0^1 = … = x_0^n.
results.note: The initialization is identical across workers because each round all workers branch off from the same global `x` which starts at `problem.x0`.

results.description: The communication interval τ is an integer ≥ 2, and the total number of iterations T is a multiple of τ.
results.evidence: In algorithms.py, tau is typed as int and used as a loop bound (e.g., `for _ in range(tau)` in run_localsgd line 58, run_scaffold line 95). All configs use tau=50 (≥ 2), tests use tau=3 (≥ 2). T = rounds * tau by construction, making T always a multiple of τ structurally. However, there is NO explicit assertion or validation that τ ≥ 2 anywhere in the codebase (no assert, no raise, no conditional check). The paper's constraint τ ≥ 2 is satisfied by the values used in experiments but is not enforced or validated in code.
results.note: The T-is-multiple-of-τ part is implicitly satisfied by the loop structure (T = rounds * tau). The τ ≥ 2 constraint is met in practice (all configs/tests use τ ≥ 2) but is not enforced. Whether this counts as "implemented" depends on whether the rubric requires explicit enforcement or merely consistent use.

results.description: The objective function is f(x) = 1/n ∑_{i=1}^n ( L(x; A_i, y_i) + λ (x^2)/(1+x^2) ) where L(x; A_i, y_i) = (n/m) ∑_{j=1}^{m_i} h(A_i(j) · x − y_i(j)), with h(·) a smoothed Huber loss defined as h(u) = 0.5 u^2 if |u| ≤ 0.5, 0.125 + 0.5(|u|−0.5) + 0.5(|u|−0.5)^2 − 0.5(|u|−0.5)^3 if 0.5 < |u| ≤ 1.0, and |u| − 0.375 if |u| > 1.0.
results.evidence: The smoothed Huber loss in src/reproduction/losses.py (smoothed_huber_value function, lines 8-19) uses thresholds 1.0 and 2.0 with formula: 0.5u² for |u|≤1.0, -(|u|-1)³/6 + 0.5u² for 1<|u|≤2.0, and 1.5|u|-7/6 for |u|>2.0. The rubric requires thresholds 0.5 and 1.0 with formula: 0.5u² for |u|≤0.5, 0.125+0.5(|u|-0.5)+0.5(|u|-0.5)²-0.5(|u|-0.5)³ for 0.5<|u|≤1.0, and |u|-0.375 for |u|>1.0. The regularizer λx²/(1+x²) IS correctly implemented (line 38), but the core smoothed Huber loss definition does not match the paper's specification in Equations (21)-(22).
results.note: The structure (regularizer form, overall objective) is similar but the specific smoothed Huber piecewise definition uses different breakpoints and polynomial coefficients than specified in the rubric.

results.description: The stepsize is tuned over the grid {0.0003, 0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3}.

results.description: The loss function is the smoothed Huber loss as defined in Appendix B.1.
results.evidence: src/reproduction/losses.py implements `smoothed_huber_value` and `smoothed_huber_grad` functions. The docstring states it is "The C2 smoothed Huber penalty h(u) from Appendix B." The piecewise definition: quadratic for |u|≤1 (0.5*u²), cubic-blended for 1<|u|≤2 (-(|u|-1)³/6 + 0.5*u²), linear for |u|>2 (1.5*|u| − 7/6). The `WorkerObjective` class only accepts `loss="smoothed-huber"` and raises ValueError otherwise, enforcing this loss across all synthetic experiments including LocalSGD parameter dependence.
results.note: The CLAIMS.json does not explicitly label exp3_local_sgd_param_dependence, but the WorkerObjective used by all synthetic experiments enforces the smoothed Huber loss exclusively.

results.description: The regularizer is x^2/(1+x^2) with regularization parameter λ = 0.01 in the basic setting.
results.evidence: losses.py lines 36-38: `regularizer_value(x, rho)` computes `rho * np.sum(x * x / (1.0 + x * x))`, matching x^2/(1+x^2). All LocalSGD configs (fig1_localsgd_delta.json, appendix_localsgd_delta.json, appendix_localsgd_zeta.json) set `rho: 0.01` in the common/basic setting. The datasets.py is titled 'Synthetic heterogeneous regression instances'; the 'local' dataset corresponds to the paper's synthetic setting.
results.note: The specific experiment_id 'exp3_local_sgd_param_dependence' does not exist in the repository (closest matches: appendix_localsgd_rho/delta/zeta). The dataset is named 'local' in code, not 'synthetic'. Both the regularizer formula and λ=0.01 are otherwise correctly implemented for LocalSGD experiments.

results.description: The squared gradient norm for the ζ and δ dependence panels is evaluated at the 50th communication round (iteration 2500).
results.evidence: configs/appendix_localsgd_zeta.json and configs/appendix_localsgd_delta.json both set "rounds": 50 and "tau": 50. In run_formal.py, "final_grad_norm_sq" = result["history"][-1]. In src/reproduction/algorithms.py, run_localsgd records history[0] before training, then appends after each of 'rounds' communication rounds, so history[-1] = history[50] = after the 50th communication round. With tau=50 local steps per round, total gradient steps = 50×50 = 2500. The plot config (plot_appendix.json) uses "final_grad_norm_sq" from summary.csv for the zeta/delta dependence scatter plots, confirming evaluation at round 50 = iteration 2500.
results.note: The rubric uses "synthetic" as the dataset label; the repo uses dataset="local" (and "scaffold") which are both synthetic generated datasets. This naming discrepancy does not affect the verdict since both are synthetic constructions.

results.description: The squared gradient norm for the λ dependence panel is evaluated at the 10th communication round (iteration 500).
results.evidence: No experiment matching "exp3_local_sgd_param_dependence" or "λ dependence" exists in the repository. The configs directory contains only: appendix_localsgd_delta.json, appendix_localsgd_rho.json, appendix_localsgd_zeta.json (and SCAFFOLD equivalents), plus Fig 1 configs. None vary a λ parameter, none use a "synthetic" dataset label, none specify evaluation at round 10 (iteration 500). CLAIMS.json shows only 3 claims (C1–C3), none referencing λ or exp3. The run_formal.py script evaluates metrics at all rounds (0 through common["rounds"]), recording final_grad_norm_sq=result["history"][-1], which is at round 50, not round 10. With τ=50, round 10 would be iteration 500, but this evaluation point is not implemented anywhere.
results.note: The repository appears to be a reproduction of a paper about LocalSGD/SCAFFOLD with Hessian dissimilarity, but the specific λ-dependence experiment described in the rubric (exp3, Figure 2, Appendix B.2) is entirely absent from the codebase.

results.description: The experiment is run with three random seeds {111, 222, 333} and the results are averaged.

results.description: The loss function is a smoothed Huber loss with a non-convex regularizer, where the regularizer is λ_reg * ∑_{j=1}^d x_j^2/(1+x_j^2) with λ_reg=0.01.

The WorkerObjective class combines both. SCAFFOLD experiment configs (configs/appendix_scaffold_rho.json, configs/appendix_scaffold_delta.json) set "rho": 0.01 for SCAFFOLD synthetic experiments, matching λ_reg=0.01.
results.note: The experiment_id "exp4_scaffold_param_dependence" is not named exactly in the config files, but the SCAFFOLD configs with rho=0.01 on synthetic data correspond to the described setup. The loss implementation matches the paper claim exactly.

results.description: The data generation controls Hessian similarity δ by adjusting the noise in A_i and gradient similarity ζ by the variation in x_i^*.
results.evidence: In src/reproduction/datasets.py, function make_problem(): (1) Hessian similarity δ is controlled via A_i construction: for the 'scaffold' dataset, even-indexed workers use scale=sqrt(1+delta/L) and odd-indexed use scale=sqrt(1-delta/L) applied to sqrt_lambda @ Q.T (lines ~97-102). (2) Gradient similarity ζ is controlled via x_i^* variation: after generating random x_stars, bias_vectors = hessian @ x_i^* are computed, their variance spread is measured, and x_stars are rescaled by zeta/spread (lines ~104-107), directly tying ζ to the variation in x_i^*.
results.note: The claim matches exactly for the 'scaffold' dataset variant. The 'local' dataset uses spectral noise on A_i for delta instead, but for the SCAFFOLD experiment (dataset='scaffold'), the implementation matches the rubric.
